sample_unit: simulated test prompts (appeal letters per LLM)

links.outcome: Existence and relevance of literature citations in LLM-generated appeal letters
links.effect: All LLMs, including GPT-4web, were poor at supporting clinical assertions with existing, relevant, and appropriately cited primary literature.
links.quote: All LLMs, including GPT-4web, were poor at supporting clinical assertions with existing, relevant, and appropriately cited primary literature.

links.outcome: Benchmarking of LLM configurations on an intended-use task with blinded expert scoring
links.effect: GPT-4 and GPT-4web letters demonstrated superior clinical reasoning and were readier for submission than GPT-3.5 letters (p < 0.001); fine-tuned GPT-3.5ft performed worse across all domains (p < 0.001).
links.quote: GPT-4 and GPT-4web letters demonstrated superior clinical reasoning and were readier for submission than GPT-3.5 letters (p < 0.001).

unlisted_practices: Fine-tuning an LLM on a small task-specific dataset (53 examples) worsened confabulation and performance

screen.reason: Evaluated multiple LLM models (including fine-tuned and web-search versions) on simulated clinical vignettes to draft radiotherapy insurance denial appeal letters, evaluated by expert radiation oncologists.
